This is for September 2014. Nothing really to show off in here. I only took 14 trades total in this month. I avoided a lot of trades and only took the ones that I understood. I got into some trades that were losers but I exited them quickly and realize they weren't working. My biggest trades were the GBPUSD long and a GBPAUD short. They were swing trades. Most of my trades are swing trades because of my job. Now I want to incorporate day trades because I can. I can trade the half part of the New York Session.

My goals were to be have a positive gain, every month. For the last two months I have reached my 5% goal. That might not seem a lot but for someone who has been losing even on a demo account. I made that goal because I only took trades that I understood and avoided a lot of trades. Some trades were easy to execute, had a gut feeling into them and they did work. Sometimes I saw live PA and hesitated and the set up just left my entry and ended up being "right". Emotions were a big part of me. Up to now that's something I have to work on.

I have a new goal. Is to trade every single day. At least one trade a day. I am preparing my self to trade when I do this full time, because I won't have a steady income anymore with my current job. I have to train my mind into this mode. Like it's serious. Like if I didn't trade, I won't have anything to eat and nothing to pay my rent. I realize by doing this. I am gonna make a lot of mistakes. LOTS of THEM. And hopefully I can fail my self forward to success in this business.

I decided that I want to master trading the 1m TF because I think they're best for income trading. Last month I was making more money than my current hourly rate being an employee for this medical company. I broke one of my cardinal rules in my plan. I was playing with improper risk management, I think some of you guys been there. So I took off a month off of trading and charts. I'm ready again, this time with rules set on paper. It's still developing but I have them written down on my notebook.

One of the things I'm writing are my trigger points for entry and exits so I may trade objectively. I'm just basically looking for set ups so that I can recognize in the future and trade them confidently So here I spotted a set up:

Most of the trades I take produce more than 5:1 RR or even 8:1 RR or +10:1 RR if I left them be. The rule that I have written down is that day/scalp trades have to be 2:1 RR. So I automatically take them at 2:1 RR. Now I'm grateful that I'm able to take those trades and end up in profit, but I see more potential in what I can make.

How would I know if these trades would produce more than 2:1 or less so that I can exit at BE at the least? I don't want to put a trade and just "hope" that it will keep on going. Do I look at a possible entry in the opposite direction?

like this

Now this trade was 8:1 RR, to be honest I really didn't know if price was going to get to that FTR above. I guess I am lucky because I was in the bathroom when this was happening and exited right when it reached the FTR.

Setting appropriate targets is a must for me to maximize my trades. This is my next focus of study now.

I had a PO on this level, but deleted it. I heard a poker player said before that "scared money is lost money." My goal is to trade freely as in to execute with out hesitation.

I notice this set up so many times. Where price would bounce from the last FTR level inside a compressed of stacked FTRs and the last FTR lvl is clearly distinctly separated by a big giant pole that would represent the another PAZ.

here's for today:

HTF 15m DP lvl

LTF 1m entry at DP lvl after the 3D approach

So this 15m FTR SUPPLY that EURUSD produced turned out to be a can can set up and there was many different ways to take advantage of the set up.

Price compressed back to the 15m FTR SUPPLY for the second time.

I've seen this type of set up before. Where price would 3-D to supply and would produce a reaction, when price returned to the supply again, it would bounce on the second drive as a QM lvl of the 3-D set up. I learned this from IF from one of his trade examples back then, specifically the AUDUSD trade a while ago.

and this one is a similar set up I found today.

This is the HTF 15m, showing the can can set up.

and take a look at the 2TB to the cap and the reaction.

It reacted to the QM lvl of the second drive of the 3-D set up. And another trading opporunity when a bear flag (FL supply) is created after the seemingly uptrend but compressed price action and the entry at the return.

I didn't catch any of those today because I woke up extremely late, I had work until 12 am last night. I'm training my body to get used to 6.5 hrs to 7 hrs sleep a night. This is my first trade of the day. It's a simple set up. FL supply is engulfed, with that another FL is created and entry at FTB to the new FL, my target was the opposite QM lvl and an FTR lvl.

Oh yeah, to help me with my trading I've also gotten rid of the terminal window temporarily on MT4, because when I get into a live trade I used to get distracted by the potential cash gained or loss. By releasing the need to see how much money I've made or loss, I can focus solely on the charts and the procedures of trading properly.
